business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A (P4) and the 10-K business section (P1).

quotes: We offer a variety of convenient month-to-month memberships with no long-term contracts, including:

business_model.claim: The customers are individual and family members, mostly in affluent suburban and urban areas. The 10-K reports a member median household income of $160,000.
quotes: Our member base is primarily made up of members in affluent suburban and urban locations.

quotes: Total revenue consists of Center revenue and Other revenue (each defined below).

business_model.basis: Stated: the percentages come from the release KPI table (P6) and the definition from the 10-K MD&A (P3).

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K (P1); the cancellation point is in the risk factors (P2): 'All of our members are able to cancel their membership at any time upon providing advance notice.'

business_model.basis: Stated in the earnings release (P6); the 10-Q MD&A (P4) also says membership growth is smaller than Center revenue growth.

risks.basis: The membership and revenue figures and management's explanation are stated. The pricing-resistance mechanism is inferred.

quotes: With these membership dynamics and our premium, high-use model, our growth in the number of center memberships has been smaller than our total Center revenue growth and we expect that trend to continue, including because our clubs are typically reaching their desired utilization and revenue with fewer memberships.

risks.basis: The growth rates are stated in P6. Whether this is a trend break is inferred.

quotes: Comparable center revenue growth of 8.5% to 8.7%, which includes our ramping and mature centers, increased from 7.9% to 8.3%.
